gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-lexend-tera: Woodgod has tall lowercase that nearly reaches its capitals, with wide channels cut into every bowl, giving it a vintage, commanding look. Lexend Tera spreads out beneath it.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-lexend-zetta: Lexend Zetta reads as approachable and widely tracked, its strokes a constant width from start to finish. Woodgod sits above it, vintage and commanding, with lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-montserrat-alterna: Woodgod's lowercase climbs almost to the capital line, with wide channels cut into every bowl, which gives its headings a vintage, commanding feel. It leads; Montserrat Alternates keeps the sign-painter's single-stroke sans steady.
gen-fs-bevellier-archivo: Flat and stencil-cut, Bevellier sets every stroke at a single weight, with letters packed tight and a wide-looking lowercase. Archivo follows with open, outward curves and a tall x-height that keeps the text approachable.
gen-fs-bevellier-fs-merriweather-sans: Bevellier is cut like a stencil, with every stroke the same width and sidebearings pulled very tight, so its wide lowercase sits low and graceful. Merriweather Sans stands taller beneath it.
gen-fs-bevellier-general-sans: General Sans reads with a steady pen pressure, a tall x-height filling the line and smooth curves with nothing in the way. Bevellier is the one for stencil-cut, graceful display; General Sans handles the body.
gen-fs-bevellier-manrope: Manrope has bright open gaps at the mouth of every curve, and a minimal step from capital to lowercase keeps its line uniform. Over many paragraphs it reads smoothly, never crowding the eye, while Bevellier stays a stencil-cut accent.
gen-fs-bevellier-satoshi: Stencil-flat and graceful, Bevellier packs its single-weight strokes close together. Satoshi comes in with a soaring x-height and a wide-open e, approachable where the heading is sophisticated.
gen-fs-bevellier-switzer: Stencil-cut and tightly spaced, Bevellier looks flat and graceful, with a wide-looking lowercase and squat ascenders. Switzer sits next to it as wire-like, tubular letterforms with a tall waist line, friendlier and more Swiss.
gen-fs-bevellier-work-sans: Bevellier's stencil-cut strokes all share a single weight and sit very close together, with a wide-looking lowercase and squat ascenders. Its job is graceful display; Work Sans, with its high mean line, handles the text.
